title: PRO*ACTIVE – Proactive Return-to-Work Psychotherapy for the Early Return to Employment for Patients with Depression
summary:
Depression is among the most common mental disorders in Germany and, in addition to its health-related and social consequences for affected individuals, is associated with high costs for the healthcare system. Moreover, depressive disorders are one of the most frequent causes of long-term sickness absence. Patients who are on sick leave due to this diagnosis and receive sickness benefits are often unable to work for more than six months. Delayed diagnoses and long waiting times for psychotherapy appointments postpone treatment and worsen health outcomes. In many cases, potential vocational reintegration is addressed too late or not at all during treatment.

This is where the PRO*ACTIVE project intervenes by promoting the reintegration of patients with depression into working life through a focused care approach. Patients diagnosed with depression and at risk of prolonged sickness absence are identified by health insurance providers and referred to the new care program. After verification of the diagnosis through a second-opinion procedure, participants receive timely, tailored outpatient psychotherapeutic treatment. This is followed by a return-to-work-oriented psychotherapy program that includes cognitive behavioral therapy with a workplace focus, delivered in specially certified practices.

To evaluate the effectiveness of this new therapeutic approach, the clinical course of 125 participants receiving this intervention is compared with that of 125 participants receiving standard psychotherapy. Outcomes include the number of sick leave days and changes in depressive symptoms. In addition, a health economic evaluation and a process evaluation are conducted. The project is funded for 40 months with a total budget of approximately EUR 4.1 million.

If successful, this efficient and guideline-based treatment approach has the potential to improve the health status and quality of care for patients with depression while simultaneously reducing prolonged periods of sickness absence.

interventions.name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy with a Return-to-Work Focus (RTW-CBT) (Short-Term Therapy I + Short-Term Therapy II, maximum total of 28 sessions)
Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Provided as Treatment as Usual (TAU-CBT) (Short-Term Therapy I + Short-Term Therapy II, maximum total of 24 sessions)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Statutorily insured with AOK Niedersachsen
•	Currently employed
•	Aged between 18 and 60 years
•	Currently on sick leave due to a diagnosis of depression (F32.0, F32.1, F32.2, F32.8, F32.9, F33.0, F33.1, F33.2, F33.8, F33.9, F34.1)
•	Current sickness absence of at least 42 days at the time of randomization
Exclusion criteria:
•	Risk of early retirement due to reduced earning capacity (F0, F72, F73)
•	Receipt of unemployment benefit I or citizen’s allowance (Bürgergeld)
•	Currently receiving (partial) inpatient or outpatient guideline-based psychotherapy
•	Not suitable for outpatient treatment (F0X.X, F2X.X, F7X.X)
•	As sufficient German language skills are required for psychotherapeutic treatment, individuals with German proficiency below B1 level are excluded from study participation
